gap: No result ChatGPT got states the parking-ready price of each pick (camera plus the maker's own hardwire kit, at today's store prices) or which picks stay under $100 once the kit is added: a DDPAI Mini Pro 4K with kit is $69.00, a Vantrue S1 Pro 1CH with the kit that names it is $109.98, and the VIOFO A119 Mini 2 is $159.99 before its $17.99 kit.
standout_why: Compared against carcody.com and rottenwifi.com (both cited) and dealdey.com (rank 1); dashanddrive.com (cited) could not be opened (certificate error). Carcody gives only a hypothetical ('a $15–$30 high-endurance card and a $15–$30 hardwire kit', 'A camera advertised at $89 can become a $120–$150 purchase') and no kit price for any model. Rottenwifi says only that accessories are separate and can push a camera over $100, with no figures. Dealdey gives camera-plus-card totals for Amazon models (A119 V3 about $131–$132, Kingslim E4 about $81–$82) and no hardwire kit price. None pairs a named camera with its maker's own kit price read today or says which stay under $100.
decides: It changes the pick for anyone who wants parking mode. ChatGPT's 'best front-only value', the Vantrue S1 Pro 1CH at $79.99, goes over $100 with a Vantrue kit ($109.98 with the Voltage Display kit, $104.98 with the Universal ACC kit). The VIOFO A119 Mini 2 that ChatGPT named first is $159.99 at viofo.com today, so it is out on budget before any kit. The rows that stay under $100 parking-ready are DDPAI's bundle variants (Mini Pro 4K + kit $69.00; N1 Dual + kit $89.00 and N2 Dual + kit $99.00 for front plus rear) and the Vantrue Element 1 Lite ($94.98 to $99.98 with a kit). For a shopper who only plugs into the 12 V socket, the S1 Pro 1CH still fits at $79.99. Caveat: the DDPAI and Vantrue camera prices are the brief's partner-store reads of 2026-11-21, not pages I opened myself, because both stores returned HTTP 429 on every attempt; I could not read DDPAI Mini Pro 4K specs at all.
